core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 8965-8968): pick a K-injective complex I representing M, a K-injective complex J representing L and a K-flat complex K representing K.
Define the map (proof lines 8968-8976): the canonical morphism is defined through the map Tot(Hom(J, I) tensor K) -> Hom(Hom(K, J), I) supplied by the cited evaluation lemma.

Identify the two sides (proof lines 8976-8981): by the choice of complexes the left hand side represents R-Hom(L, M) tensor^L K and the right hand side represents R-Hom(R-Hom(K, L), M), so the displayed map is a morphism in D(O) as claimed.
proof_roadmap: Choose K-injective and K-flat representatives so that both sides compute the intended derived functors.
Define the morphism through the evaluation map on the level of complexes and identify the two sides.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a ringed site and objects K, L, M of the derived category, a canonical morphism from R-Hom(L, M) tensor^L K to R-Hom(R-Hom(K, L), M), functorial in the three variables (statement lines 8964-8974). The proof (proof lines 8965-8995) chooses K-injective and K-flat representatives and defines the map through the evaluation map on the level of complexes, identifying the two sides with the required derived functors. H2: one construction with two inputs, written out in full.
